events.title: Community Paddle at Starlight Park
events.description: Join the Bronx River Alliance for a free community paddle at Starlight Park! Come see your neighborhood from the river’s perspective!This event is first come, first served with no pre-registration available.“Waves” of paddlers will enjoy the river for about 30-40 minutes, after signing waivers and receiving a brief paddling safety orientation. A total of 4 waves of participants will be able to go on-water every hour of the event (11am, 12pm, 1pm, 2pm), with a maximum of about 15 participants per wave.Staff and volunteers will be on-water to ensure safety, but please keep in mind that this is not a guided tour of the river.Minors must be accompanied by an adult. Waivers for minors will need to be signed by an adult guardian.

events.title: Concert: Maximilian Gordon, Pleasure Systems, Pierre, 3 People (DJ Set)
events.description: Maximilian Gordon, Pleasure Systems, and Pierre perform live in the magical 6BC Botanical Garden on Saturday, September 5. 3 People will be the afternoon's garden DJs. Maximilian Gordon builds rich trumpet and keyboard worlds with live loops and field recordings. Pleasure Systems is gentle and heartbreaking soft-pop and folk project of songwriter Clarke Sondermann. Pierre is the project of violist and singer Isabella Bustanoby, who infuses contemporary indie songwriting with a medieval aesthetic. 3 People is the experimental DJ duo of writer Daniel Felsenthal and musician Maximilian Gordon. Their soundscapes blend ambient, jazz, and poetry.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: "Prior Occupants" Artist Talk & Special Screening with Alison Nguyen
events.description: Join us for the premiere of Alison Nguyen’s new film Prior Occupants, co-commissioned by High Line Art and CHANEL Culture Fund. Following the screening, Nguyen will be joined in conversation by High Line Art Associate Curator, Taylor Zakarin, to discuss her practice and this exciting new work.This event is rain or shine. Although advance RSVP is full, walk-up visitors will be welcome if the event is not at capacity._____________________________________________________________________________________________________Alison Nguyen is a visual artist working across video, installation, performance, and sculpture. Using approaches of speculative fiction, documentary research, and embodied performance, Nguyen creates works that reconsider how narratives operate within the individual, the institution, the archive, and within the politics of cultural memory.In her compelling new film for High Line Originals, co-commissioned with CHANEL Culture Fund, Nguyen explores the obscure nuclear history of Westbeth Artist Housing’s building—the former headquarters for Bell Laboratories, a research facility tied to the development of communication technologies and, later, the atomic bomb. Inspired by a severed fragment of the original High Line freight rail left embedded in Westbeth’s facade, and the High Line’s own history of transformation, Nguyen reflects on the historical narratives that persist—and those quietly erased—within sites of adaptive reuse.Long before Westbeth’s conversion into a historic public housing community for artists in 1970, the site was occupied by Western Electric and later Bell Labs—a crucible of innovation where critical cinema, telecommunications, and military technologies were researched, including components later used in the development of the atomic bomb. Both Bell Labs and Westbeth Artist Housing are places created to pursue large, even utopian ideals. In the case of the former, technological innovation; in the case of the latter government-funded artist housing. Prior Occupants explores what remains of the pursuit of these ideals, how the surrounding architecture has shaped its inhabitants, and the contradictions of present-day Westbeth in the context of the High Line’s surrounding neighborhood.Prior Occupants is an assemblage of audiovisual material including sculpturally re-filmed archival documents, choreographed performance sequences, and layered fragments of audio interviews with the very residents and architects who have shaped Westbeth and the High Line. Through this collage of voices and textures, the artist explores individual and collective relationships to place, technological acceleration, and mortality, and foregrounds the ways in which the structures of the past quietly haunt our future-present. Questioning the relationship between ruination and cultural production, the work asks: What does it mean to stage the decay of an industrial past within public environments and within public artist housing? What role does nature play in these acts of preservation? Nguyen’s film weaves together infrastructure, memory, and technology to consider how the legacy of the nuclear age continues to shape our collective experiences, and positions the High Line not just as a space for leisure, but as an active conduit of our historical consciousness.Part of High Line Channel, High Line Originals is High Line Art’s commissioning program for artists working in time-based media. This initiative invites emerging or underrecognized US-based artists, nominated by a trusted group of contemporary curators, to submit a proposal for a new video work that considers the context of the park in a meaningful way and will resonate with our diverse audience.High Line Originals launched in 2019 with Tourmaline’s Salacia, which is now held in the Museum of Modern Art’s permanent collection. Other past commissions include Onyeka Igwe’s The Miracle on George Green (2021), and Alicia Mersy’s NYC Wisdom (2024). In 2025, High Line Art partnered with CHANEL Culture Fund, and together co-commissioned Frank WANG Yefeng’s Groundless Flower – ? (2025).

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Poetry at Bryant Park Reading Room
events.description: Cai Sherley (he/him) is a Black trans poet-educator with roots in Boston, MA. Cai is a two-time Pushcart Prize nominee, with work published or forthcoming in Best New Poets, swamp pink, Peach Mag, and Tupelo, as well as the anthology I Feel Nothing Like Good: Poets Against Genocide from Taylor & Co Books. His work centers Black transmasculine life, past and present, in the United States, and has found homes at The Watering Hole, Brooklyn Poets, Tin House, LAMBDA, and the Fine Arts Work Center. Cai is a member of the Crossroads Writers Collective and Trans Corner Poets, and the proud stepfather of two sphinxes. He is the author of Out of Yearning, selected by Kay Ulanday Barrett as part of SRP’s 2026 Bridges Series.Charlie Lou Evans (he/they) grew up in a small town in New Jersey, went to college at Virginia Tech, spent two summers thru-hiking the east and west coast, and now lives in Bellingham, Washington. His first chapbook, Gay Sex, celebrates the liberating power of queer love and was released by Sibling Rivalry Press this June. He explores gender and sexuality through poetry and finds it most fulfilling when others see themselves in their work.JC Andrews (she/her) is a lesbian poet from Springfield, Arkansas. Her work can be found in Gulf Coast, The Massachusetts Review, Waxwing, and elsewhere. Her debut collection, Of an Ilk, was a finalist for the 2024 National Poetry Series and won the 2026 Yale Series of Younger Poets competition. It will be published with Yale University Press in April 2027. Her chapbook, Trillion Amber Trumpets, was published with Sibling Rivalry Press in April 2026 as part of the Arkansas Queer Poet Series.Kaitlin Hsu ?? (she/her/?) is a queer Taiwanese poet who believes in a free Palestine. A 2025 Lambda Literary Fellow and 2024 Margins Fellow at the Asian American Writers Workshop, she has also received support from Brooklyn Poets, genARTS Silicon Valley, the Mendocino Coast Writers Conference, and more. She is the author of the chapbook Paper Dolls (Sibling Rivalry Press), selected by Kay Ulanday Barrett as part of SRP’s 2026 Bridges Series. Her work can be found most recently in A Public Space, Poet Lore, and Peach Mag. She currently works at Kaya Press as an associate editor and development coordinator.Toni Garcia-Butler (he/they) is a poet and community artist-educator rooted in Little Rock, Arkansas. He approaches his craft as a memory keeper, believing that poets and artists can be creative cultural archivists. His writing and art center the lived experiences of his people: Black, Fil-am, southern, trans/queer, and everyone existing within the intersections. As a facilitator, Toni encourages folks to empower themselves through DIY publishing/zinemaking, personal narrative, and creative joy. In 2025, Toni was named Best Poet in Arkansas by the Arkansas Times. His chapbook, D I Y Body, was published with Sibling Rivalry Press in June 2026 as part of the Arkansas Queer Poet Series.Hosted by:Bryan Borland is the founding publisher of Sibling Rivalry Press and founding editor of Assaracus: A Journal of Gay and Queer Poetry. He is the author of multiple poetry collections, including Brotherful, a finalist for the Thom Gunn Award for Gay Poetry, and DIG, a finalist for the Lambda Literary Award in Gay Poetry and Stonewall Honor Book as honored by the American Library Association. His most recent book is Listen, Kid: Selected and New Poems (2010-2026).Kay Ulanday Barrett is a poet, essayist, and cultural strategist. Barrett is a 2024 Disabled Futures fellow awarded by The Ford Foundation, Mellon Foundation, and United States Artists. They are the winner of the 2022 Foundation for Contemporary Arts Cy Twombly Award for Poetry, a winner of the 2022 Next Book Residency with Tin House, a James Baldwin Fellowship at MacDowell, residencies at Baldwin for the Arts, and Millay Arts awarded by Lambda Literary. Their second book, More Than Organs (Sibling Rivalry Press, 2020) received a 2021 Stonewall Honor Book Award by the American Library Association and was a Lambda Literary Award Finalist. They have featured at the United Nations, Lincoln Center, Hemispheric Institute, The Whitney, MoMA, Symphony Space, the Ford Foundation, Brooklyn Museum, Princeton, Columbia, Yale, Manchester PRIDE, Sesame Street, & more.

events.title: Summer Movies in the Park | The Namesake
events.description: An immigrant family maintains a delicate balancing act between the traditions of their native India and blending into American culture.Prospect Park Alliance, Fort Greene Park Conservancy, and Rooftop Films announce Summer Movies in the Park, presented by NewYork-Presbyterian. This free, outdoor movie series in Prospect Park and Fort Greene Park takes place on Wednesday nights this summer, with screenings on August 5th and August 12th in Prospect Park, and August 26th and September 9th in Fort Greene Park. September 9: The Namesake (PG-13) – 20th Anniversary Screening6:00 PM: Lawn Opens8:30 PM: Film BeginsDirections: Fort Greene Park, Central Lawn at Washington Park and Dekalb Avenue EntranceThe Namesake (PG-13)– 20th Anniversary ScreeningMira Nair | 2006 | US, Japan, India | 122 minsIn this film by Mira Nair, based on the novel by Jhumpa Lahiri, the Ganguli family maintain a delicate balancing act between honoring the traditions of their native India and blending into American culture after moving from Calcutta to New York. The films will begin shortly after sundown; come early to picnic and enjoy pre-movie entertainment. Please note that the movie may be cancelled in the case of inclement weather. Attendees will be notified via Eventbrite and the Prospect Park and Fort Greene Park social media channels.This series is presented through support of NewYork-Presbyterian.

events.title: Know Your Rights
events.description: This workshop offers immigrant families and community members practical information about their legal rights, a broad overview of how the U.S. immigration system operates, and how to prepare for immigration-related emergencies. Participants will learn about the roles of agencies such as ICE, local law enforcement, and how to access resources from the Mayor's Office of Immigration Affairs. Topics include post-detention support, legal and social resources, emergency/family preparedness, avoiding immigration fraud, and worksite immigration enforcement actions. The workshop aims to equip participants with reliable information and practical tools to support their safety and preparedness.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. events.title: Project Evergreen at Phoenix Community Garden Volunteer Workday
events.description: The Phoenix Community Garden in Brooklyn is 1/2 acre of green goodness in the Ocean Hill/Brownsville section of Brooklyn. Phoenix gardeners have changed a formerly vacant lot into a pastoral space where community members come together to make their garden grow. The garden is open to all members of the community. The garden grows nearly 2,000 pounds of beans, corn, collards, bitter melon, tomatoes, zucchini, herbs and callaloo to feed the neighborhood.  The garden provides fresh food, green space, and community to folks in Ocean Hill-Brownsville. Project EverGreen’s GreenCare for Communities initiative transforms public green spaces, making communities healthier and more sustainable. events.title: Public Gallery Tour
events.description: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site. When exhibitions are on view in the spring, summer, and fall, Gallery Greeters lead public exhibition tours on Thursdays and Saturdays at 2PM, certain dates excluded. events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.title: Jackie O and John Perreault at Snug Harbor: A Literary Portrait
events.description: Jackie O and John Perreault at Snug Harbor: A Literary Portrait Featuring guest speakers:   Wayne Koestenbaum, Author of Jackie Under My Skin and Andy Warhol: A Biography Daniel Rothbart, artist currently exhibiting at Snug Harbor and friend of John Perreault On the 50th anniversary of Snug Harbor opening its doors to the community after the transition from Sailors’ Snug Harbor into Snug Harbor Cultural Center on September 12, 1976, join us for an intimate literary reading that traces the legacies of two essential figures within the Snug Harbor story.  When: Saturday, September 12, 2026 |  3:00 PM – 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building CAdmission: Free (Registration Required) Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and John Perreault were each instrumental in shaping the story of Snug Harbor Cultural Center. In the mid-1970s, when after being saved from demolition, the former sailors’ home faced an uncertain future, Kennedy toured the site on behalf of the Municipal Art Society, lending her influence to the preservation effort. Later, she famously piloted the Staten Island Ferry back to Manhattan. A decade later, Perreault became one of the first professional curators at the Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art at Snug Harbor (1985–1989), where he championed Staten Island artists such as Julia Healy, Elizabeth Egbert, and Cynthia Mailman, while also presenting off-island figures including Nancy Spero, Judy Chicago, and Gillian Jagger. Though they moved in different circles, Andy Warhol forms a compelling link between them. As chief art critic for The Village Voice in the 1960s and ’70s, Perreault became a key chronicler of Pop Art and a close friend of Warhol—at one point speaking with him nightly for nearly two years. Warhol’s Jackie series, based on images of Kennedy  before and after the assassination, was among the works Perreault reviewed with particular attention. Jackie herself maintained a cordial relationship with Warhol and shared friends in New York’s art and fashion worlds, including Halston and Truman Capote. In the summer of 1972, she and her, Lee Radziwill, along with their children, stayed at Warhol’s Eothen estate in Montauk. Another point of resonance between Jackie O and John Perreault is fashion. Kennedy helped define 1960s style through the so-called “Camelot” look—pillbox hats, tailored shift dresses, and Oleg Cassini-designed suits—later evolving into her signature “Jackie O” ensemble of oversized sunglasses, headscarves, and Gucci handbags. Perrealut, in turn, approached fashion as an artistic medium. In 1969, with Hannah Weine and Eduardo Costa, he co-organized the Fashion Show Poetry Event, a hybrid of runway, performance, and text. Twenty artists designed garments worn by fellow artists and poets, accompanied by live music and recorded readings written specifically for each look. Participants included Andy Warhol, James Lee Byars, Alex Katz, Marisol, Claes Oldenburg, and James Rosenquist, among others.    Artist and writer Wayne Koestenbaum is the author of Jackie Under My Skin, a book about Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and Andy Warhol: A Biography. In 1998, he curated an exhibition titled Bathroom at the Thomas Healy Gallery, exploring themes of the body, voyeurism, and personal territory, which included work by John Perreault. Artist and writer Daniel Rothbart met Perreault in 1999, and the two maintained a close friendship and ongoing creative dialogue until Perreault’s death in 2015, frequently writing about one another’s work. Perreault included Rothbart in The Ritual Feast at KK Projects in New Orleans in 2008. Drawing on personal experience and longstanding engagement with their subjects, Koestenbaum and Rothbart will reflect on the intertwined legacies of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and John Perreault, and consider how each helped shape the cultural history of Snug Harbor. This literary reading is part of our Serpentine Sybils public art exhibition on view at the Pond and the Glasshouse

Activities will focus on running techniques for sprints and relays and will introduce other track and field activities like long jump, hurdles, and long-distance running. Program Dates:  Every SaturdaySpring: 4/11 – 6/20, no program on 5/23 Fall:  9/12 – 10/31 Registration is required on LeagueApps with City Parks Foundation. Location: Thomas Jefferson ParkFor inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Monarchs and Milkweed: Creating and Connecting Habitat for Monarch Butterflies
events.description: The monarch butterfly is one of North America’s most iconic and beloved species. With vibrant orange-and-black wings, the butterflies can be observed in NYC’s parks and gardens from late spring until fall, when they take to the sky to make a remarkable migration, traveling south to the mountains of Mexico where they will spend the winter. Unfortunately, monarch populations have declined significantly in recent decades for a number of reasons, including the loss of milkweed plants--the only plant monarch caterpillars eat. But there’s good news: we can help monarchs by planting native milkweed species and restoring and connecting pollinator habitat throughout their migratory flyway. During this workshop, learn about the monarch’s life cycle, its impressive multi-generational 3,000 mile migration, and how to help them thrive in NYC green spaces. Attendees will be able to take home native milkweed or butterfly nectar plants for their gardens.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. Served on the Kate French Terrace, weather permitting, or in our quaint Tea Room at historic Wave Hill House, Afternoon Teas are provided by our exclusive partner Great Performances whose menu uses local and seasonal ingredients, inspired from their own organic farm, Katchkie Farm.Enjoy the indulgence of a traditional tea service including:Tea SandwichesSmoked Salmon with Taramasalata, Pickled Fennel, Black BreadChicken Salad Pinwheel on a Whole Wheat WrapCucumber & Watercress on Fresh SourdoughSmoked Turkey with Garlic Thyme Mayo & Cheddar BiscuitScones & CakesAssorted Seasonal Scones and Tea Cakes, with Clotted Cream and JamSweetsAssorted Macarons; Fruit Tartlet; Flourless Chocolate Cake BitesA selection of teas or House Made CocoaEnhance your Afternoon Tea with a glass of sparkling wine! A minimum of 2 guests and 7-day advanced booking are required. Complimentary admission to Wave Hill is included with purchase of tea package.For bookings, and additional information, please click here.

events.title: Hart Island Tour (North Island)
events.description: Hart Island is the largest public cemetery in the country and has served New York City since 1869. While Hart Island is currently only used for city burials, the island is deeply connected to New York City institutions. It has served many uses since the 19th Century, including a military training ground, a quarantine station, a psychiatric hospital, a reform school, a rehabilitation facility, a missile base, and a jail.Join the Urban Park Rangers to explore Hart Island's unique past, present, and future. Participants are chosen by lottery. Lottery registration opens on Wednesday September 2, 2026 and ends Thursday September 3, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.  Please Note:-You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same account. Anyone who was not registered will not be permitted to attend.-  If you are selected for the program, you will receive a series of emails confirming your selection and must respond as soon as possible to avoid forfeiting your spot. - Hart Island is only accessible via ferry. Selected participants will be provided details regarding program arrival and other specifics.- There are no indoor facilities, restrooms or drinking fountains on Hart Island. There are portable restrooms on the island.- This tour covers historical context of Hart Island and is about two hours of walking, some parts on uneven terrain. Please dress appropriately for the weather and the terrain.- Program may be cancelled due to inclement weather at the discretion of ferry operations.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Poetry at Bryant Park Reading Room
events.description: Chelsea Whitton is the author of Bear Trap (Dancing Girl Press, 2018) and Wonder Wheel, published by LSU Press in March of this year. She holds a PhD from the University of Cincinnati and an MFA in Poetry from The New School. Her poetry and prose have appeared in many of print and online publications, including Beloit Poetry Journal, Copper Nickel, Cream City Review, Poetry Ireland, The Atlanta Review, and Forklift-Ohio. Her work has been a finalist for the Gearhart Prize, and the Frost Place and Adrienne Richard awards for poetry. She is the recipient of the 2018 Sandy Crimmins National Poetry Prize. Raised in the Carolinas, she spent her twenties in New York and now lives in Southwestern Ohio, where she teaches at the Art Academy of Cincinnati.Dilruba “Ruba” Ahmed is the author of Bring Now the Angels (Pitt Poetry), with poems featured in New York Times Magazine, The Slowdown, and Poetry Unbound.  Her debut book, Dhaka Dust (Graywolf Press), won the Bakeless Prize.  Her poems have appeared in Kenyon Review, New England Review, Ploughshares, and Virginia Quarterly Review.  Her work has also been anthologized in Best American Poetry, Halal If You Hear Me, New Moons: Contemporary Writing by North American Muslims, They Rise Like a Wave: An Anthology of Asian American Women Poets, and elsewhere. Ahmed received The Florida Review’s Editors’ Award, a Dorothy Sargent Rosenberg Memorial Prize, and the Katharine Bakeless Nason Fellowship awarded by the Bread Loaf Writers Conference. In 2021, she joined the faculty at Warren Wilson College’s MFA Program for Writers.Matthew Yeager’s poems have appeared in American Poetry Review, Poem-a-Day, and elsewhere, as well as numerous anthologies, including Best American Poetry 2005, 2010, and 2024, The Strategic Poet, and Twenty Years of PoemoftheWeek.com. “A Big Ball of Foil in a Small NY Apartment,” his micro-budget short film, was an official selection at eleven film festivals in 2009-2010, picking up three awards. His “Poem to First Love” has appeared in online features in O, The Oprah Magazine, Good Housekeeping, Newsweek, Brides, and elsewhere. Other distinctions include the Barthelme Prize in short prose and multiple fellowships to both MacDowell and Yaddo. The co-curator of the KGB Monday Night Poetry Series from 2011-2017, Yeager’s first book, Like That (Forklift Books, 2016), received a starred review from Publishers Weekly. He teaches adjunct and lives in Cincinnati with his wife Chelsea Whitton and their twin sons Hank and Pete.Sahar Muradi is author of the collection OCTOBERS, selected by Naomi Shihab Nye for the 2022 Donald Hall Prize for Poetry and a finalist for the National Poetry Series. She is author of the chapbooks [ G A T E S ], Ask Hafiz, and A Garden Beyond My Hand, and co-editor of two anthologies: One Story, Thirty Stories: An Anthology of Contemporary Afghan American Literature, and EMERGENC(Y): Writing Afghan Lives Beyond the Forever War, An Anthology of Writing from Afghanistan and its Diaspora. Her writing has been supported by Asian American Writers’ Workshop, Bethany Arts Community, Blue Mountain Center, Kundiman, and Sustainable Arts Foundation. Sahar directs the arts education programs at City Lore and dearly believes in the bottom of the rice pot.

events.title: Flamboyants! by La Compagnie Tilawcis, Musical Concert
events.description: A concert version of an original musical connecting the Creole cultures of Réunion Island, Puerto Rico, and New Orleans.Réunion Island-based theater company Tilawcis brings their latest work, Flamboyants!, on a North American tour this fall. This work of documentary theater with music explores the remarkable intersections of Creole culture and identity between the geographically distant communities of Réunion Island, New Orleans, and Puerto Rico through music, storytelling, and gorgeous projections.Five languages are spoken on stage, and nearly a dozen instruments are played, fusing maloya, bomba, and Mardi Gras Indians songs. The piece explores themes of memory, identity, resilience, connection, and cultural transmission through the prism of the Creole experience. It shines a light on the richness of Creole cultures and their capacity to overcome historical oppression.Flamboyants! is a philosophy as much as it is a work of theater. Despite the 10,000 miles that separate Réunion from New Orleans, the Creole languages spoken in those two places are close linguistic cousins. Maloya musicians use the same Canna indica seeds in their kayamb instrument (a rectangular rattle made of sugar cane tubes) as bomba musicians use to create maracas in Puerto Rico. While the ties between these cultures have long been lost, their ancient, resilient wisdom, connected by the African diaspora, once again finds a home on stage in the celebration of Creole identity that is Flamboyants!Plot Summary: Réunion Island. While a cyclone rages, a man curses his name before throwing himself in the Indian Ocean. He has no idea what repercussions this action will have on the other side of the world. From Puerto Rico to New Orleans, Creole peoples will unite to teach him his true history. A work of musical theater, documentary and fictional, even fantastical in certain moments, Flamboyants! asks us to interrogate what stories our own names carry, the ways we’re interconnected, and the cultural resilience of those who fight to not be forgotten.

events.title: Guided House Tour: Healthcare in Tredwell Times
events.description: Curious about healthcare in the 19th century and the illnesses that affected New Yorkers during that era? On this afternoon tour, we’ll explore the diseases and treatments common in 19th century New York. Drawing from firsthand accounts and historical sources, we’ll learn about major outbreaks of cholera, diphtheria, typhoid fever, and the recorded causes of death within the Tredwell family, along with the types of medical care they might have received. This tour will also highlight how the Civil War spurred significant medical advancements and changed the way physicians and nurses were trained.60-75 minutes.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.title: In the Distortion of Celestial Privacy, a Door Left Open in the Mind
events.description: Set within the living landscape of 6BC Botanical Garden, this third annual iteration, curated by Sarah Viviana Valdez, brings together the sculptural practices of Ori Carlin, Erin Lingard, and Lizzy Chemel. The artists span materials and techniques, notably including wood-fired ceramics, metal, concrete, salvaged materials and stained glass mirages. Their works share a common sentiment toward incredible craftsmanship deriving from botany, memory, and family histories. Throughout the garden's labyrinth, each location and placement of these pieces will similarly act as an embroidery unifying the rhythms and quiet transformations to shape their own narratives. Beginning in the afternoon and unfolding toward sundown, the exhibition will culminate with closing performances by Sky Axe, Karol Konstancia with ensemble, and Fillan Fernando. These performers honor traditions of myth, folklore, songwriting, choral a cappella, and poetry. The intent is to offer gifts that extend the exhibition’s exploration of memory and storytelling. We invite visitors to wander through a space where sculpture, sound, and movement become small openings into remembrance and shared imagination. For folks who feel compelled, the curator will offer tours throughout the day. Enjoy these presented moments of pause where the private worlds we carry within us are invited to briefly open onto the garden and one another.

events.title: Managing Invasive Plants in Community Gardens
events.description: This workshop introduces gardeners to practical strategies for identifying, managing, and preventing invasive plant species in community garden spaces. Participants will learn how to recognize common invasive plants found in urban gardens, understand their impact on local ecosystems, and explore effective methods for control and long-term management. Topics include plant identification, seasonal timing for removal, mechanical and cultural management techniques, restoration practices after removal, and discussion of which approaches are most effective in urban growing environments. The session is designed to help gardeners make informed decisions and build healthier, more resilient garden spaces. Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Morgan Walk: River Park
events.description: Join historian Terrell L. Armistead in a special tour along the Bronx River at River Park as they share the ecological stories and community histories of the Bronx River. Led in honor of Morgan Powell, a founding member of the Bronx River Restoration and a passionate advocate for the reclamation of the Bronx River. His research has been fundamental in sharing the lesser known histories of Black and Brown Bronxites and their contributions to the eco-cultural history of NYC. You can read more of these histories can be found in detail in his blog called the Bronx Sankofa.Often much is known about the middle to Africa but less is known of the original “highways” of colonial New York, its rivers! This tour will highlight the importance of the Bronx River to indigenous Americans and its role in both enslavement and freedom for African slaves. We will also discuss the critical role of the river systems to our communities today and how Morgan Powell’s impact continues to outlive him. Note: This is part of a series of Bronx Black History Walking Tours hosted by Terrell Armistead.

events.title: National Dance Day
events.description: Celebrate National Dance Day with a guided walk through Fort Tryon Park featuring dance, live music & poetry!Meet at Broadway and Dongan Place Entrance at 3PM | Audience Members Guided Through the Park On Wheelchair Accessible Pathways | Walking ProductionCelebrate National Dance Day with an immersive, multi-disciplinary arts production in Fort Tryon Park! A guided walk through the park leads audience members to view Uptown Dance Collective’s (UDC) “Alterations and Repairs: Nature and Us” with dance, music, and spoken word all woven into the landscape of the parkland. Audience members will also take a little journey to Brazil and learn Samba dance at the end of the walk and some Bomba from Puerto Rico along the way.UDC dance artists Lisa Green, Amy Kail, Navarra Novy-Williams will be joined by Shanik Garcia, Juan Usera, Paul Thompson, and Rishauna Zumberg. This group of dance artists collectively draw from diverse traditions including Afro-Brazilian, Afro-Puertorican, and European and U.S. Modern Dance in creating and performing their dances. John Ehlis, Matthew Gonzales, and Jessica Lurie perform original music on Saxophone, Flute, Guitar, and Drums; and poets Alison Stone and Peter Bulow share poems created for the day. Alexis Camacho, Victoria Lopez, and Valerie Quito from The Center Dance Studio in Inwood will also join us this year!We encourage our audience to bring light pillows, blankets, or folding chairs you can easily carry as we go from site to site.“Alterations and Repairs: Nature and Us” is made possible with support from The City Parks Foundation’s Green Fund, The Harkness Foundation for Dance, The Greenacre Foundation, and The Medical Center Neighborhood Fund. This event brings the arts to the outdoors—inviting you to witness, move and connect.Click Here to go to Uptown Dance Collective’s WebsiteRain date: Saturday September 26

events.title: Uncovering Uptown History: A Guided Walking Tour
events.description: The Morris-Jumel Mansion brings New York history to life in the brand-new “Uncovering Uptown History” guided walking tour!Manhattan's oldest residence, the Morris-Jumel Mansion, brings Uptown Manhattan history to life in the brand-new “Uncovering Uptown History” guided walking tour!Morris-Jumel Mansion guides bring you along a series of hidden historic gems of New York history in the brand-new “Uncovering Uptown History” guided walking tour: a 90-minute, one-mile mobile experience beginning at the Morris-Jumel Mansion and ending at Trinity Cemetery on Broadway and 155th. Spanning over 260 years, this tour illuminates little-known corners of the Revolutionary War, the Gilded and Industrial Ages, the Harlem Renaissance, and more, connecting the paths of legendary figures with the ones we walk today. Perfect for locals, hard to impress history buffs, and tourists looking beyond well-known sites of New York City.Dress seasonably and wear your walking shoes. The walk is considered easy to moderately challenging.All tours will begin at the Morris-Jumel Mansion (65 Jumel Terrace, New York, New York 10032) in the Colonial Era Kitchen (Basement Entrance)September 2026 Tours9/59/12 (NO 1:30 PM tour due to Family and Community Day)9/199/26Two tour times to choose from! Tour 1: 10:30 AM – 12:00 PMTour 2: 1:30 PM – 3:00 PM (No 1:30 PM tour on 2nd Saturday of each month, please be sure to check in advance to see if tours are running.
